newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil tracks crude, volatility knocks trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil tracks crude, volatility knocks trade.

text.p: Fuel oil strengthened on Monday on the back of firmer crude after a late rally on Friday, but activity was muted as dealers watched futures drfit lower.
"People just want to let crude settle and calm down, before dipping their toes into the market," said one trader.
High sulphur barges traded around $116-117 fob a tonne, up $5 on Friday amid moderate bunker demand, the high prices putting off all but those dealers who were very short of material.
Cargoes were also firmer, pegged around $115-116 cif NWE, but little physical trade was seen. The wide spread between NWE and the Med narrowed today with Med prices only $1 or so higher.

Russian material, while more thinly offered than previously, was still available. Three cargoes were already on the water with four set to load this week. An M-100 with 1.7 water was sold at $111.50 while E-4s were put around formula +$3-3.50.

Wet low sulphur cracked gained with the support of paper. $124-125.50 was talked for November and $125.50 understood done for Dec. Traders said physical cargoes were very close to paper. A 45,000 tonne cargo was on offer for a 20-22 November loading.
